children: Asian equities advanced on Monday, September 7, tracking gains on Wall Street at the end of last week, even as fresh hostilities between the United States and Iran raised investor concerns.
The broad-based rally lifted major regional benchmarks, though sentiment in India pointed towards a softer opening.

South Korea's Kospi led the region, jumping 3.16%. Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 1.90%, while the broader Topix index added 0.76%. The MSCI Asia Pacific index rose 1.1% in early trade, with South Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics driving much of the gain.

Hang Seng futures held largely steady. In India, however, the GIFT Nifty traded lower, signalling that the domestic market could open near the 23,900 mark, in contrast with the upbeat mood elsewhere in Asia.

According to a Bloomberg report, the rally traced its roots to Friday's session in the US, when the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.2%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged 3.4%, supported by strength in technology and semiconductor chip stocks. That momentum carried through to Asian trading, particularly benefiting semiconductor-linked names.

The US dollar eased slightly in early trade, while the Japanese yen strengthened 0.3% to 155.82 per dollar, building on a gain of more than 2% the previous week as carry trades unwound amid expectations of further Bank of Japan rate increases.
The offshore yuan was little changed at 6.7064 per dollar.

Oil prices, meanwhile, jumped after Iran and the US exchanged attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. Brent crude rose as much as 1% to touch $96.9 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate breached $90 to trade close to $92 a barrel.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said it had struck three oil tankers using an unauthorised route through the strait, along with several US-linked vessels, in response to earlier American strikes on Iranian tankers. The IRGC added that it had also targeted a US naval drone and an unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter the waterway.
Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaee, said Tehran would declare a new restricted zone outside the strait in the coming days, according to a Bloomberg report.

title: Asian stocks rise as chip rally lifts Kospi over 3%; oil jumps on Hormuz tanker strikes
